summary: Steel lookout tower above the Eyrie House ruins on Mount Nonotuck in Mt. Tom State Reservation; NHLR-registered May 2026 as US 1822; no build date found.

facts.design: Steel tower with red paint, base about 8 feet square, wide top platform that cantilevers off the frame (NHLR)
facts.status_note: NHLR says the tower is less well maintained than neighboring towers and a small derelict shed stands at its base; no structural assessment found

access.note: Reached by trail off Reservation Road in Mt. Tom State Reservation (NHLR). The summit auto road is closed to vehicles (Wikipedia). The Register does not say whether the tower itself may be climbed.

visit.trail_note: Trail off Reservation Road; the stairs are very steep, nearly a ladder (NHLR). Ask DCR whether climbing is permitted before going up.

events.note: Eyrie House summit hotel opened on Mount Nonotuck; a Mt. Tom history site lists a lookout tower among its amenities. The Register says the present tower was not part of the hotel.
Fire destroyed the Eyrie House hotel complex; the Register says it was started to cremate horses. This is about the hotel, not the tower.
Property annexed to the adjacent Mt. Tom State Reservation
Registered May 25, 2026 as US 1822, MA 49; nominated by Tori Bonazoli

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Mt. Tom history site lists a lookout tower among the 1861 hotel's amenities, but the Register says the present tower was not part of the hotel. Both can be true, since the present tower may be a later structure. No build date for the present tower was found, so the story says so.

notes_for_editor: Only the Register describes the tower itself; it gives no build year, builder, or fire-lookout service, and the record's kind is unknown. The Wikipedia article has no tower content. Access to the tower top and whether climbing is permitted were not confirmed, so the visit note says to ask DCR. Do not encourage climbing. The 1901 hotel fire and the 1905 annexation are about the hotel, not the tower.
